selected_goal_name: Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup
selected_goal_description: Replace the disposable perspective test camera with a fixed orthographic isometric camera configuration matching the GDD's Diablo-1/Ultima-Online-inspired fixed 2.5D isometric presentation.
implementation_summary: Modified DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.BuildCamera() (the sole method responsible for the Main Camera in the door prototype scene) to replace the perspective test camera with a fixed orthographic isometric camera. The camera now sets `Camera.orthographic = true` with an `orthographicSize` of 8, and uses a fixed transform (position (10,10,-10), rotation Euler(30,45,0)) — the classic 30/45 dimetric isometric angle consistent with the GDD's Diablo 1 / Ultima Online-inspired presentation and with Unity's conventional "Isometric Z as Y" tilemap authoring angle referenced in the GDD's Runtime Implementation section. No rotation-input or camera-follow component was added, so the camera transform stays hard-fixed by the scene builder and cannot rotate freely — matching the candidate's "fixed" requirement. No Tilemap authoring or sprite-sorting work was touched, per the candidate's explicit scope exclusion. The disposable primitive Floor/Walls/Door/Player test room was left untouched as the visual verification target, also per scope.
tests_added: Build_MainCamera_IsFixedOrthographicIsometric — asserts camera.orthographic is true, orthographicSize > 0, camera rotation matches the fixed 30/45/0 isometric angle (not the old perspective angle), and no Rotate/Orbit-named component is attached to the camera hierarchy.
Build_RunTwice_MainCameraStaysSingleAndFixed — asserts re-running the scene builder does not duplicate the Main Camera and it remains orthographic.

requirements_satisfied: Perspective test camera at (0,8,-8) rotated (45,0,0) replaced with an orthographic camera.
Camera uses a fixed isometric angle (30/45 dimetric) and fixed position, matching the GDD's Diablo 1 / Ultima Online-inspired fixed 2.5D isometric presentation.
Camera transform is hard-coded by the scene builder with no rotation-input/orbit component, so it cannot rotate freely.
Change is scoped to camera projection/transform only — no Tilemap authoring or sprite-sorting configuration was added.
Existing disposable primitive Floor/Walls test room left in place as the visual verification target, unchanged.
remaining_work: Human/Unity execution: open the project in the Unity Editor, run the scene builder, and visually confirm the isometric framing against the existing test room (cannot be done in this container without a Unity executable).
Human/Unity execution: run the Edit Mode Test Runner to confirm the two new camera tests and existing tests pass.
notes: The whole DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs file appears heavily modified in a plain `git diff` only because it is tracked with CRLF line endings that read as full-file trailing-whitespace/line changes to git's default diff; `git diff -w` isolates the real change to the intended ~18-line camera edit plus the doc comment/constants. This CRLF condition predates this task and was left untouched. Orthographic size (8) and camera offset distance (10,10,-10) were chosen to keep the existing disposable Floor (20x20 units)/Walls/Door/Player test room framed in view for visual verification; these are reasonable defaults for a fixed isometric camera and are not part of any GDD-specified numeric requirement, so a human may want to tune them once real isometric Tilemap art exists in a later task.
